title: Efficient Serving of LLM Applications with Probabilistic Demand Modeling
technique: Probabilistic Demand Graph (PDGraph) of application resource demand; Gittins-policy scheduling order and backend (KV/LoRA/docker) prewarming

optimized_metrics.evidence: Hermes applies the Gittins policy to determine the scheduling order that can minimize the average application completion time.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: metric is the average application completion time (ACT)

optimized_metrics.evidence: if the expected deadline is provided—maximize the goodput (number of applications that complete before the deadline)

headline_claim.text: reducing the average completion time by over 70% and the P95 completion time by over 80%

reported_metrics.where: Fig 9a, 10a (average ACT vs workload intensity), Fig 12-14

metric_definitions.definition_quote: users primarily focus on the application completion time—that is, the time when the high-quality output (like the valid code) is finally returned [51]. Therefore, the efficiency objective shall be set at the application level, i.e., minimize the average application completion time (ACT)
metric_definitions.notes: Application = DAG/loop of LLM calls plus non-LLM tasks (docker code execution, retrieval); ACT measured per application from submission to final return, including queueing in the global queue.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: maximize the goodput (number of applications that complete before the deadline)
metric_definitions.notes: Goodput counted in applications, not tokens.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Deadline Satisfaction Ratio (DSR, meaning the ratio of applications that can complete before the specified deadline)
metric_definitions.notes: Deadlines = original execution time scaled by 1.2x (tight), 1.5x (modest), 2x (loose).

slo_spec: Deadlines assigned per application by scaling original execution time by random factors 1.2x (tight), 1.5x (modest), 2x (loose), following prior studies; metric is DSR.
load_regime: application submission window sweep (10/15/30 min = 3x/2x/1x workload intensity); 300 apps for LLaMA2-7B, 3000 for LLaMA3-70B
tradeoff_acknowledged: Prewarming trades resource wastage for latency reduction (Fig 14 avg latency change vs resource consumption); naive SRPT fails under demand uncertainty.
hardware: single-GPU server with 1x A100-PCIe-40GB; multi-GPU server with 8 NVIDIA GPUs
workloads: benchmark suite of LLM applications of small/medium/large duration (e.g. KBQAV, CG, PE, DM, MRS)
extractor_notes: Program-level only: ACT (mean, P95) and DSR; no TTFT/TPOT/token throughput. Mean ACT is the scheduling target (Gittins minimizes expected completion time); P95 appears as evaluation. Quality not part of the objective (though ACT is defined up to 'high-quality output'). | TAIL AUDIT 2026-10-06: demoted PROGRAM_JCT@P95 (non-tail entry kept)

load_class_quote: The average ACT with varying application arrival intensities. [Fig 7: application submission window sweep 10/15/30 min, bursty real-trace arrivals]
